questions.question: Describe Nelson Mandela's childhood, including where he was born and grew up.
questions.expected_answer: He was born on 18 July 1918 in Mvezo, in the Eastern Cape, and named Rolihlahla. He grew up in Qunu, herding cattle and sheep. A teacher gave him the name Nelson. After his father died, he lived with the Thembu regent, where he learnt that a leader should listen to everyone.

questions.question: What happened to Mandela between 1962 and 1990?
questions.expected_answer: He was arrested in 1962, and at the Rivonia Trial in 1964 he was sentenced to life in prison. He spent twenty-seven years in prison, eighteen of them on Robben Island, before he was released on 11 February 1990.

questions.question: Give three reasons why Nelson Mandela is an example of a good leader.
questions.expected_answer: He listened to people, worked with a team such as Oliver Tambo and Walter Sisulu, was brave, was dedicated to freedom for over fifty years, sacrificed his freedom and family life, chose peace and reconciliation instead of revenge, and stepped down after one term.
